title: Post-Tito collective federal presidency
summary: After Tito's real death, the collective federal presidency exercised the head-of-state function under the constitutional succession system.
political_significance: Defining the counterfactual role of a public Tito and the legality of federal orders.
limitations: Do not claim that a real 1980 successor presidency governed under a living Tito.

title: 1980 dinar devaluation and IMF arrangement
summary: Authorities devalued the dinar in June and a Fund standby arrangement supported external adjustment.
political_significance: Foreign debt and exchange rate pressure are institutional constraints on federal governance.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Polish shipyard strikes and independent Solidarity organization
summary: Strikes and negotiations led to the independent Solidarity labour movement in September 1980.
political_significance: Yugoslav workers and authorities could compare labour self-organization with events elsewhere in socialist Europe.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Three-year IMF stand-by arrangement
summary: The Fund and Yugoslav authorities agreed to a three-year standby amid debt and foreign-exchange constraints.
political_significance: Economic sovereignty, state finance, shortages and external creditors affected political choices.
limitations: Dates represent programme period, not a single event.

title: Greece joins European Communities
summary: Greece joined the EC as its tenth member.
political_significance: Yugoslavia gained an EC member along its southern frontier; trade and border diplomacy offer period context.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: 1981 Kosovo student protests escalate
summary: Student protests beginning on 11 March expanded into demands including republic status for Kosovo; authorities used force and deployed security units.
political_significance: Pivotal dispute over constitutional autonomy and state responses; fatalities and totals are disputed.
limitations: Differing sources dispute casualties; avoid precise figures and collective blame.

title: Martial law imposed in Poland
summary: Polish authorities imposed martial law in December 1981 following Solidarity's growth.
political_significance: Useful international example of tension between Communist authorities and independent mass organization.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: External lending confidence and debt-service pressures worsen
summary: Commercial lenders tightened Yugoslavia-related terms amid regional debt concerns; IMF records identify funding and debt-service strains.
political_significance: Gives historically grounded background to resource scarcity and inter-republic economic disputes.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Milka Planinc elected federal prime minister
summary: Federal parliament elected Milka Planinc as prime minister; the government described nonalignment, federal unity and economic problems as priorities.
political_significance: Leadership and executive documents provide a historical institutional grammar for the Unaligned.
limitations: Party/state institutional continuity may change when Tito survives.

title: Seventh Non-Aligned summit in New Delhi
summary: The seventh NAM summit met in New Delhi in 1983, continuing diplomatic discussions among states outside formal Cold War blocs.
political_significance: Demonstrates Yugoslavia's nonalignment as an active international network, not isolation.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Sarajevo political trial of Muslim intellectuals
summary: Proceedings against Alija Izetbegović and other defendants began in July 1983, concluding with convictions in August; rights and legitimacy of the prosecution were contested.
political_significance: Illustrates political surveillance, religious and ideological rights disputes and criminal-law controversies in late socialism.
limitations: Source is associated with a defendant; independently verify legal proceedings and sentencing details.

title: Madrid CSCE follow-up meeting concludes
summary: The CSCE's Madrid follow-up process concluded in September 1983.
political_significance: Helsinki-process diplomacy and human-rights discussions offer sources for international public positions.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Bulgarian campaign against Turkish minority intensifies
summary: State pressure to change names and suppress Turkish minority cultural identity increased from 1984, with a mass exodus later in 1989.
political_significance: Contemporary minority-rights tensions in a Yugoslav neighboring state shaped regional diplomatic and human-rights discussion.
limitations: A multi-year policy period; do not conflate minorities, state authorities and refugees.

title: Sarajevo Winter Olympics as diplomatic stage
summary: Yugoslavia hosted the XIV Winter Olympic Games; major international attention and civil/military security logistics accompanied the event.
political_significance: Public international staging matters to the credibility of government broadcasts in the fictional assassination year.
source_institution: Olympic Committee of Bosnia and Herzegovina
limitations: Game may shift event effects following surviving-Tito premise; do not equate Olympic security with the fictional cover-up.

title: Mikhail Gorbachev assumes Soviet leadership
summary: Gorbachev became Soviet leader in March 1985 and later pursued perestroika, glasnost and arms-control diplomacy.
political_significance: Changes the Red Directorate's fictional Cold War inspiration without making it the actual Soviet government.
source_institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Death of Enver Hoxha
summary: Albanian ruler Enver Hoxha died on 11 April 1985, ending his personal leadership of an isolated neighboring socialist state.
political_significance: Provides regional context for Kosovo/Albania frontier relations and Albania's distinct political system.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Five EC states sign Schengen Agreement
summary: Five European states signed the Schengen Agreement for the gradual removal of internal border checks.
political_significance: Contrasts western integration with Yugoslav customs and transit systems; actual implementation came later.
limitations: Do not depict 1985 Schengen as immediate borderless travel across all of Europe.

title: Eighth Non-Aligned summit in Harare
summary: The eighth NAM summit convened in Harare in 1986.
political_significance: Nonaligned diplomacy is not passive neutrality; convention schedules matter to fictional intelligence objectives.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Spain and Portugal join the EC
summary: Spain and Portugal became the eleventh and twelfth EC members.
political_significance: Demonstrates Western European integration reshaping Yugoslavia's trading environment.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Slobodan Milošević becomes Serbian Communist Party leader
summary: Milošević rose to the presidency of the League of Communists of Serbia in May 1986.
political_significance: Begins major shift in power competition inside the Serbian republic.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Draft SANU Memorandum becomes public
summary: A draft memorandum associated with members of the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts emerged publicly in September 1986 and became central to political controversy.
political_significance: Useful for studying competing constitutional narratives and nationalist discourse.
source_institution: UÇK History and Memory (interpretation is movement-affiliated)
limitations: Distinguish leaked draft authorship from official collective endorsement and treat interpretive framing as source-affiliated.

title: Vienna CSCE follow-up review opens
summary: The CSCE Vienna review began in November 1986 and continued into January 1989.
political_significance: Documents the European human-rights and security architecture around Yugoslav diplomacy.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Nova revija issue 57: Slovenian national programme essays
summary: Issue 57 published contributions envisioning self-determination, constitutional rights and political pluralism.
political_significance: Relevant to conflicting constitutional proposals and politically active print culture.
limitations: It is a collection of essays, not an already enacted independence declaration.

title: Slovenian writers' public forum on constitutional changes
summary: The Writers' Association organized a forum about amendments to the federal constitution.
political_significance: Shows constitutional debate extending beyond republican political offices.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Milošević addresses Serb grievances in Kosovo
summary: At Kosovo Polje, Milošević spoke to Kosovo Serb demonstrators amid tensions over provincial governance and alleged mistreatment.
political_significance: Major public media and mobilization turning point, with contested interpretations of grievance claims.
limitations: Allegations voiced by demonstrators are not independent proof of general population conduct.

title: Single European Act enters into force
summary: The Single European Act entered into force and advanced the EC's single-market programme and foreign-policy cooperation.
political_significance: Strategic context for trade, customs and western economic orientation.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Agrokomerc financial scandal becomes public
summary: Reporting and investigations over unauthorized financial instruments at Agrokomerc became public in August 1987, followed by high-level accountability debates.
political_significance: Directly connects enterprise finance, regional development, the press and political officeholders.
limitations: A participant's recollections inform chronology; accusations and individual culpability require independent confirmation.

title: Eighth Session Serbian party leadership struggle
summary: The Eighth Session of the Serbian League of Communists Central Committee strengthened Milošević's control and marginalized Ivan Stambolić's allies.
political_significance: A case of intra-party conflict and political media management within a federal republic.
limitations: Year/month supported; avoid invented session-day precision.

title: Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty signed
summary: The US and USSR signed the INF Treaty eliminating a class of ground-launched intermediate-range missiles.
political_significance: Nuclear diplomacy can influence fictional factions' deterrence narratives without inventing actual Yugoslav nuclear weapons.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Litostroj workers' strike and independent organizing
summary: Litostroj workers struck over pay and challenged the political and self-management order; a strike committee and calls for independent unions and a social-democratic organization emerged.
political_significance: Economic decline intersects with new political mobilization and labour agency.
source_institution: Archives of the Republic of Slovenia
limitations: Keep actual workers distinct from fictional factions.

title: Republic–JNA disputes over jurisdiction intensify
summary: Public controversy concerning military prosecution and political authority grew during 1988 in Slovenia.
political_significance: Distinguish ordinary Yugoslav service personnel from the separate fictional clandestine authority.
limitations: Cross-reference JBTZ record; intentionally broad rather than an additional fabricated military action.

title: Ivan Stambolić removed from Serbian presidency
summary: Milošević's faction displaced Ivan Stambolić in early 1988.
political_significance: Marks shifting Serbian republican institutions independently from federal leadership.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Writers' constitution project published
summary: A draft of a new Slovenian constitutional order prepared by writers and sociologists was published in April 1988.
political_significance: Shows alternative constitutional programmes emerging ahead of later amendments.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: JBTZ affair: military-secret arrests
summary: Arrests and military proceedings against Janez Janša, Ivan Borštner, David Tasič and Franci Zavrl fuelled a public civil-rights crisis.
political_significance: A sharp distinction between military legal authority, civilian journalism and republican institutions.
limitations: Do not depict historical defendants or journalists as fictional secret assassins.

title: Committee for Defence of Human Rights mobilizes
summary: Civil-rights activism and an organized defence committee grew around the military trial.
political_significance: Institutionally grounded civilian response and parallel information networks.
limitations: Exact committee formation day requires an item-level source.

title: Novi Sad demonstrations force provincial leadership's resignation
summary: Mass rallies in Novi Sad culminated in resignation of Vojvodina's leadership on 6 October 1988.
political_significance: Key provincial power shift in the anti-bureaucratic movement.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Trepča miners march in protest
summary: Mining workers travelled to Priština to oppose changes in provincial leadership and autonomy.
political_significance: Labor, autonomy and industrial transport converge in a politically contested local setting.
limitations: Exact date differs by event phase; consult original mining and press records.

title: Dismissal of Kosovo Communist Party leadership
summary: Kosovo's party leadership was removed during escalating Serbia–province constitutional conflict.
political_significance: Leadership change precipitated further Albanian protests and mine worker mobilization.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Federal constitutional amendments open path to Serbian provincial changes
summary: Federal parliamentary amendments passed in November 1988 and were followed by Serbian constitutional revision affecting Kosovo and Vojvodina.
political_significance: A constitutionally contested pathway from federal to republican and provincial jurisdiction.
limitations: Source chronology from rights-report; review exact legal texts before scripting constitutional mechanics.

title: Mikulić federal cabinet resigns amid crisis
summary: The federal government under Branko Mikulić resigned in late 1988 during economic and political difficulties.
political_significance: Shows weakening federal executive authority preceding Ante Marković's reform government.
limitations: Month is approximate; avoid exact day and succession-date assertions.

title: Ante Marković heads new federal reform government
summary: Ante Marković assumed federal executive leadership in 1989 and pursued economic stabilization and market-oriented reforms.
political_significance: Reformist federal institutions create a counterweight to political fragmentation.
limitations: Appointment date not fixed from this source; avoid a day-specific claim.

title: Tenth Congress of the League of Communists of Macedonia signals reform
summary: During the party's late-November 1989 congress and leadership transition, Macedonia's communist elite moved toward political pluralism and a new approach to federal negotiations.
political_significance: Macedonia followed its own republican trajectory, with distinct priorities from Serbia and Slovenia.
limitations: A 1999 comparative academic study documents the reformist leadership shift; exact day-by-day congress proceedings should be checked against contemporaneous Macedonian press.

title: Montenegrin leadership resigns amid mass demonstrations
summary: Montenegro's leadership resigned in January 1989 amid anti-bureaucratic demonstrations and a republic-level political shift.
political_significance: Demonstrates that federal crisis affected Montenegro directly, not only Serbia and Slovenia.
limitations: Period city name is Titograd; chronology of competing demonstrations should be checked by local archives.

title: Vienna CSCE Concluding Document adopted
summary: The Vienna CSCE follow-up concluded with an agreed document addressing security and human dimension questions.
political_significance: Contemporary text for plausible treaty and embassy archives.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Federal special security measures in Kosovo
summary: Yugoslav federal authorities deployed special security measures during strikes and resistance to proposed autonomy reductions.
political_significance: JNA, police and federal jurisdiction must be distinguished from local protest participants.
limitations: Use precise legal language and avoid collapsing all emergency measures into identical forces.

title: Polish Round Table negotiations
summary: Communist authorities and Solidarity engaged in negotiations beginning February 1989 and agreed on political reforms.
political_significance: One of the region's key models of negotiated transition.
source_institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Kosovo Assembly votes under pressure on constitutional amendments
summary: The Kosovo Assembly accepted proposed restrictions on autonomy amid heavily contested proceedings and security presence.
political_significance: Constitutional legitimacy and contested record-keeping are historically relevant design motifs.
limitations: Legality, quorum and free consent have been contested; do not call vote unanimous or uncontested.

title: Serbia adopts autonomy-limiting constitutional amendments
area: SR Serbia / SAP Kosovo / SAP Vojvodina
summary: The Serbian Assembly approved constitutional changes reducing the powers of Kosovo and Vojvodina; protests followed.
political_significance: Major federal–provincial jurisdictional change in the late-1980s crisis.
limitations: Describe reductions in autonomy rather than imply the republics/provinces had identical status.

title: Bosnia and Herzegovina constitutional amendments
summary: The republic's assembly history records 38 amendments adopted in April 1989 that changed its electoral and political rules.
political_significance: Important distinct Bosnian constitutional transition before multiparty-party formations in 1990.
source_institution: Parliamentary Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina
limitations: Do not retrospectively insert parties established in 1990.

title: Turkish minority protests and large-scale forced departures
summary: Mass protests against assimilation in Bulgaria were suppressed and hundreds of thousands of ethnic Turks left or were driven toward Turkey in 1989.
political_significance: Major humanitarian and diplomatic tension in Yugoslavia's southeastern neighborhood.
limitations: Human-rights report includes sourced estimates; do not convert its figures into exact game claims.

title: Slovenian May Declaration read publicly
summary: Tone Pavček read a declaration advocating Slovenian sovereignty at a gathering in Ljubljana; it appeared in Delo on 10 May.
political_significance: A well-documented turning point in public constitutional politics and mass gatherings.
limitations: Preserve real political message separately from in-game misinformation.

title: Slobodan Milošević becomes President of Serbian Presidency
summary: Milošević assumed the presidency of Serbia's collective republican presidency in May 1989.
political_significance: Important distinction between republican presidency and federal Yugoslav office.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Croatian Social Liberal Alliance founded
summary: The Hrvatski socijalno-liberalni savez was founded in May 1989, becoming part of the emerging multiparty political landscape.
political_significance: Documents Croatian pluralism distinct from Slovenian movements and federal party leadership.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Poland's partially free elections
summary: Partially free parliamentary elections in Poland produced a substantial Solidarity victory.
political_significance: News from the region changed the perceived durability of one-party systems.
source_institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Croatian Democratic Union founded
summary: The HDZ held its founding assembly on 17 June 1989 with Franjo Tuđman as founding leader.
political_significance: Political organizations began competing for Croatia's post-one-party future.
limitations: Party self-description is not a neutral assessment; corroborate specifics with an independent history.

title: Six-hundredth anniversary Kosovo battle commemoration and political speech
summary: Milošević spoke at the 28 June 1989 anniversary commemoration at Gazimestan amid intense constitutional and national politics.
political_significance: Major symbolically charged rally and televised political event.
limitations: Avoid disputed or sensationalized claims about speech and crowd size without qualified independent sources.

title: Pan-European Picnic border opening
summary: A temporary authorized opening of the Austro-Hungarian border allowed many East Germans to move west.
political_significance: Directly relevant to Yugoslavia's northern border environment and shifting Iron Curtain.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Ninth Non-Aligned summit hosted in Belgrade
summary: Belgrade hosted the ninth NAM summit and issued final documents circulated through the United Nations.
political_significance: A late-decade moment of visible Yugoslav diplomacy before its actual 1990s dissolution.
limitations: This event already appears in visual catalogue; this separate row indexes its political function.

title: Hungary opens its border for East Germans
summary: Hungary permitted East German refugees to leave through Austria beginning overnight 10–11 September.
political_significance: Change in neighboring states' border controls and Cold War transit routes.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Slovenian republican constitutional amendments adopted
summary: The Slovenian Assembly adopted amendments safeguarding republican constitutional prerogatives and enabling political pluralism.
political_significance: Crucial tension between republic and federal legal authority.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Yugoslav inflation accelerates into hyperinflation
summary: An IMF study documents late-1989 hyperinflation and subsequent anti-inflation policy.
political_significance: Economic stress changes citizen purchasing and confidence, not automatically battlefield prices.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Berlin Wall border crossings open
summary: East German authorities' announcement was followed by mass crossing and opening of Berlin border controls on 9 November.
political_significance: A major diplomatic and broadcast background event in POLITIKA's fictional 1989 finale.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Todor Zhivkov removed as Bulgarian party leader
summary: The Bulgarian Communist Party Central Committee removed Zhivkov on 10 November 1989.
political_significance: Directly changes leadership of a Yugoslav neighbor and the southern-east political context.
limitations: Retrospective/official sources may have an institutional perspective; verify independent corroboration for contested interpretations.

title: Croatian Communist leadership accepts multiparty turn
summary: By late 1989, reform-minded Croatian League of Communists leadership moved toward competitive elections.
political_significance: Rival reform processes within Croatia and Yugoslav federal institutions.
limitations: Elections themselves occurred in spring 1990.

title: DEMOS opposition coalition formed
summary: Opposition organizations formed the Democratic Opposition of Slovenia as an electoral coalition in December 1989.
political_significance: Alternative organized political networks develop before 1990 elections.
source_institution: Museum of Contemporary History of Slovenia
limitations: The 1990 electoral result is outside the archive time window.

title: Federal anti-inflation stabilization package announced
summary: Marković's government announced a package including dinar conversion, exchange-rate reform and temporary price/wage controls on 18 December 1989.
political_significance: A contemporaneous shift in economic administration and personal purchasing power.
limitations: Actual effects extended into 1990 and differ from fictional game-resource prices.

title: Romanian revolution topples Ceaușescu
summary: Mass demonstrations and defections brought the Romanian government down on 22 December; Nicolae and Elena Ceaușescu were executed on 25 December.
political_significance: An immediate change in political and security conditions across Yugoslavia's eastern frontier.
limitations: Unlike peaceful negotiated transitions, violence and contested responsibility require cautious treatment.

title: Democratic League of Kosovo founded
summary: Albanian intellectuals formed the Democratic League of Kosovo under Ibrahim Rugova in December 1989.
political_significance: Emergent organized civilian opposition following Kosovo's constitutional crisis.
source_institution: UÇK History and Memory (interpretation is movement-affiliated)
limitations: Movement-affiliated historical source; confirm organizational details with independent scholarship.
